word-guitar.def: a musical instrument with strings that you play with your fingers or a pick

word-piano.def: a large musical instrument with black and white keys that you press with your fingers

word-violin.def: a small wooden instrument with four strings that you play with a bow

word-drums.def: a set of round instruments that you hit with sticks to make a beat

word-flute.def: a thin metal instrument that you hold sideways and blow across to play

word-trumpet.def: a brass instrument with three buttons that makes a loud, bright sound when you blow into it

word-saxophone.def: a curved metal instrument with a reed, often played in jazz

word-cello.def: a large string instrument that you play sitting down, holding it between your knees

word-bass-guitar.def: a large electric string instrument that plays very low notes in a band

word-accordion.def: a box-shaped instrument that you squeeze and stretch while pressing keys or buttons

word-microphone.def: a device that picks up your voice or other sounds so they can be recorded or made louder

word-loudspeaker.def: a device that plays sound so that many people can hear it

word-melody.def: a series of notes that sound pleasant together and are easy to remember

word-rhythm.def: the pattern of strong and weak beats in music or speech

word-note-music.def: a single sound in music with a particular pitch and length

word-chord.def: three or more notes played at the same time

word-music-scale.def: a series of eight notes that go up or down in a fixed order

word-chorus.def: the part of a song that is repeated after each verse

word-album.def: a set of songs released together on a disc or online

word-band.def: a group of people who play music together

word-orchestra.def: a large group of musicians who play classical pieces together, led by a conductor

word-choir.def: a group of people who sing together

word-conductor-music.def: the person who stands in front of an orchestra and leads it with hand movements

word-composer.def: a person who writes pieces of music

word-dj.def: a person who plays recorded music at parties, in clubs or on the radio

word-stage.def: the raised platform in a theater or hall where performers stand

word-audience.def: the people who sit and watch or listen to a show or concert

word-rehearsal.def: a practice of a show or concert before the real performance

word-compose.def: to write a piece of music

word-tune-instrument.def: to adjust an instrument so that it plays the correct notes

word-sheet-music.def: printed pages showing the notes of a song for a player to read

word-genre.def: a type of art, writing or music with a particular style

word-classical-music.def: the traditional Western style of composed pieces for orchestras and solo players, such as Bach or Mozart

word-pop-music.def: popular songs with a catchy beat that are often played on the radio

word-rock-music.def: a loud style of songs with electric guitars and strong drums

word-jazz.def: a style that grew out of African American communities, with improvised solos and lively rhythm

word-folk-music.def: traditional songs of a country or region, passed down over many years

word-hip-hop.def: a style with rhymed words spoken over a strong beat

word-electronic-music.def: sounds and songs made with computers and synthesizers

word-opera.def: a play in which the actors sing all the words, with an orchestra playing

word-musical.def: a show or film in which the story is told with songs and dance

word-playlist.def: a list of songs chosen to be played one after another

word-whistle.def: to make a high sound by blowing air through your lips

word-hum.def: to sing a tune with your lips closed

word-vinyl-record.def: a flat black disc that plays music when a needle moves over it

word-instrument.def: a thing such as a guitar or piano that you play to make music

word-ceili.gl: céilí: Irish social gathering with traditional music, song and group dancing

word-mod-gaelic.gl: mòd: Scottish Gaelic festival of song, music, poetry and speech
